q: The surge impedance of a transmission line is:
options: Ratio of voltage to current under surge (travelling-wave) conditions
explanation: Surge (characteristic) impedance Zc = √(L/C) is the ratio of the voltage wave to the current wave travelling along the line — about 400 Ω for overhead lines and 40 Ω for cables.

q: The depletion region of a PN junction is formed by:
options: Immobile (fixed) ionised donor and acceptor atoms
explanation: Near the junction, electrons and holes recombine and leave behind fixed positive donor ions (n side) and negative acceptor ions (p side). These immobile charges form the depletion layer and its barrier field.

reported.note: The source key said "mobile" donor and acceptor ions; the ions in the depletion region are immobile — corrected.

q: The main function of a starter in a DC motor is to:
explanation: At standstill there is no back EMF, so Ia = V/Ra would be many times rated current. The starter inserts series resistance that is cut out as speed (and back EMF) builds up.

q: The efficiency of a transformer is maximum when:
options: Iron loss is greater than copper loss
Copper loss is greater than iron loss
explanation: Efficiency peaks when the variable (copper, I²R) loss equals the constant (iron) loss, i.e. at the load fraction x = √(Pi/Pcu,FL).

q: In transmission lines, skin effect increases with:
explanation: Skin depth δ = √(2ρ/ωμ) falls as frequency rises, so current crowds to the surface and effective AC resistance increases. It is also larger for thicker conductors.

q: The purpose of a surge (lightning) arrester in a substation is to:
options: Protect equipment from lightning and switching overvoltages
explanation: An arrester (ZnO) is non-conducting at normal voltage; on a surge it conducts and diverts the energy to earth, clamping the voltage below the equipment insulation level (BIL).

q: The function of a choke coil in a fluorescent tube light is to:
options: Limit the current (and give the starting voltage kick)
explanation: The choke (ballast) is an inductor in series: it produces the high-voltage kick when the starter opens, then limits the tube current because the arc has negative resistance.

q: The core of a transformer is laminated to reduce:
explanation: Thin insulated laminations cut the paths of circulating eddy currents; eddy loss ∝ (lamination thickness)². Hysteresis loss is reduced by the core material (silicon steel), not by laminating.

q: The power factor of a purely inductive circuit is:
explanation: Current lags voltage by 90°, so cos 90° = 0: the circuit takes no average (real) power, only reactive power.

q: In a 3-phase system, the phase difference between the voltages of any two phases is:
explanation: A balanced three-phase supply has three equal voltages displaced 360°/3 = 120° apart (phase sequence RYB).

q: The insulation traditionally used in high-voltage underground cables is:
explanation: Classic HV cables use oil- or mass-impregnated paper; modern ones use XLPE. PVC is limited to low voltage (≈ up to 3.3–11 kV) because of high dielectric loss and poor thermal rating.

reported.note: The source key said PVC, which is a low-voltage insulation; the textbook answer for HV cables is impregnated paper — corrected.

q: The main function of a breather in a transformer is to:
options: Remove moisture from the air entering the conservator
explanation: As oil expands and contracts the conservator "breathes". The silica-gel breather dries the incoming air so moisture does not spoil the oil’s dielectric strength. Blue gel turns pink when saturated.

q: In a series RLC circuit, the impedance at resonance is:
explanation: At resonance XL = XC, the reactances cancel and Z = R, the minimum value, so the current is maximum. (A parallel resonant circuit is the opposite: maximum impedance.)

q: Which component stores electrical energy in an electric field?
explanation: A capacitor stores W = ½CV² in the electric field between its plates; an inductor stores ½LI² in a magnetic field; a resistor only dissipates.

q: Corona in overhead transmission lines can be reduced by:
explanation: Corona depends on the surface field. A larger conductor radius (or bundled conductors) and wider spacing both reduce the field, raising the disruptive critical voltage.

q: The primary and secondary windings of a transformer are linked by:
explanation: The windings are electrically isolated; energy passes through the mutual flux in the core (Faraday’s law), which is why a transformer also gives galvanic isolation.

q: Which of these instruments can measure alternating current?
explanation: A hot-wire instrument responds to I²R heating, so it reads true RMS on AC or DC. A PMMC meter’s torque averages to zero on AC unless a rectifier is added.

q: The voltage across a resistor and the current through it are:
explanation: For a pure resistance v = iR at every instant, so voltage and current peak together (phase angle 0°, power factor 1).

q: The controlling torque in a moving-coil (PMMC) instrument is provided by:
explanation: Two phosphor-bronze hair springs give a controlling torque proportional to deflection (and also carry current to the coil). Damping is by eddy currents in the aluminium former.

q: The term "load factor" in power systems is defined as:
explanation: Load factor = average load ÷ maximum demand over a period (always ≤ 1). A high load factor means plant capacity is used well, lowering cost per kWh. (Connected load / maximum demand is the reciprocal of demand factor.)

q: In a large synchronous generator (alternator), the rotating part is the:
explanation: Large alternators use a stationary armature and a rotating DC field: the high-voltage, high-current armature is easier to insulate and connect when it does not rotate, and only low-power excitation passes through slip rings.

q: For a 220 kV system, the highest system voltage for which equipment is rated is:
explanation: IEC standard voltages: nominal 220 kV → highest system voltage Um = 245 kV (similarly 132 → 145 kV, 500 → 550 kV). Insulation levels (BIL) are chosen for Um.

q: The dielectric strength of air at normal temperature and pressure is approximately:
explanation: About 30 kV/cm peak (21.1 kV/cm RMS) = 3 kV/mm. It falls with lower air density (altitude, heat), which is why corona is worse in hills and hot weather.

q: The Ferranti effect is:
options: Rise of receiving-end voltage above sending-end voltage at light or no load
explanation: Line charging current (leading) flowing through the series inductance raises the receiving-end voltage on long, lightly loaded lines. Shunt reactors are used to control it.

q: The most commonly used material for fuse wire is:
explanation: Tin–lead (≈63/37) has a low melting point and suitable resistivity for rewirable fuses. Silver is used in high-rupturing-capacity (HRC) cartridge fuses for its stable characteristics.

q: A Zener diode is primarily used for:
explanation: In reverse breakdown the Zener voltage stays almost constant over a wide current range, so it is used as a shunt voltage regulator and voltage reference.

q: The main function of a rectifier is to:
explanation: A rectifier uses diodes (or thyristors) to pass current in one direction only. DC→AC is an inverter; AC→AC at another frequency is a cycloconverter.

q: A centre-tapped full-wave rectifier uses how many diodes?
explanation: The centre-tapped version needs 2 diodes (each conducts on alternate half-cycles); the bridge full-wave rectifier needs 4 diodes but no centre tap. Each diode in the centre-tap circuit must withstand PIV = 2Vm.

q: The unit of capacitance is the:
explanation: Farad = coulomb per volt (C = Q/V). Henry is inductance, tesla is flux density.

q: The Buchholz relay is used for the protection of:
explanation: It sits in the pipe between the tank and conservator of oil-filled transformers (above ≈500 kVA). Slow gas build-up from incipient faults gives an alarm; a violent oil surge from a severe internal fault trips the breaker.

q: The frequency of the voltage generated by a 4-pole alternator running at 1500 rpm is:
explanation: f = 50 Hz

q: In a hydroelectric plant, the turbine converts the energy of water into:
explanation: Potential energy of the head becomes kinetic energy in the penstock; the turbine converts it into mechanical (shaft) energy, and the generator then produces electricity.

q: Which of the following is a renewable energy source?
explanation: Solar (like hydro and wind) is replenished naturally; coal, oil and gas are finite fossil fuels.

q: Power is transmitted at high voltage mainly to reduce the:
explanation: For the same power P = √3 VI cosφ, raising V lowers I; losses I²R fall with 1/V², and smaller conductors can be used.

q: The power factor of a purely capacitive circuit is:
explanation: Current leads voltage by 90°, so cos 90° = 0: no real power is consumed. "Leading" describes the current, but the power factor value is zero.

reported.note: The source key said "1 leading"; a pure capacitor has power factor zero (leading) — corrected.

q: The Ferranti effect is most prominent in:
explanation: Charging current grows with line length, so the receiving-end voltage rise is significant only on long (> 250 km) EHV lines, especially at no load.

q: A DC generator converts:
explanation: The prime mover turns the armature in the field; by Faraday’s law an EMF is induced, and the commutator delivers it as DC.

q: The purpose of the commutator in a DC machine is to:
options: Reverse the current in each armature coil as it passes the brushes
explanation: The armature EMF is alternating inside each coil; the commutator (a mechanical rectifier) reverses each coil’s connection at the neutral axis so the brush output is unidirectional (and, in a motor, torque stays in one direction).

q: Which type of motor is traditionally used for electric traction (trains)?
explanation: A series motor gives very high starting torque (T ∝ Ia² below saturation) and automatically slows on heavy load, ideal for traction. Modern trains increasingly use inverter-fed induction motors.

q: The slip of an induction motor is zero when the rotor runs at:
explanation: s = (Ns − Nr)/Ns = 0 only when Nr = Ns. Then no EMF is induced in the rotor and no torque develops, so an induction motor never quite reaches synchronous speed by itself.

q: The no-load current of a transformer is:
options: Small and in phase with the voltage
Small and lagging the voltage by a large angle
explanation: It is only 2–5 % of rated current and mostly magnetising, so it lags the voltage by about 75–85° (no-load power factor ≈ 0.1–0.2).

q: The short-circuit test on a transformer is used to determine:
explanation: With the secondary shorted, rated current flows at a few per cent of rated voltage, so core flux and iron loss are negligible: the wattmeter reads copper loss, and Vsc/Isc gives the equivalent impedance.

q: A galvanometer can be converted into an ammeter by connecting a:
explanation: A low shunt Rsh = Ig·G/(I − Ig) bypasses most of the current. A high series resistance would instead make it a voltmeter.

q: The SI unit of electric charge is the:
explanation: One coulomb is the charge carried by 1 A in 1 s (Q = It), about 6.24 × 10¹⁸ electrons.

q: The working principle of a moving-coil instrument is based on the:
explanation: A current-carrying coil in the field of a permanent magnet experiences a force (F = BIL), giving a deflecting torque proportional to current — hence a uniform scale.

q: In control systems, negative feedback is mainly used to:
explanation: Feeding the output back and comparing it with the reference reduces error and sensitivity to parameter changes and disturbances, at the cost of overall gain (and possible stability issues if not designed well).

q: On a Bode magnitude plot, a single (simple) pole causes a slope of:
explanation: Each simple pole adds −20 dB/decade (−6 dB/octave) beyond its corner frequency; each zero adds +20 dB/decade. Two poles give −40 dB/decade.

q: The bandwidth of an amplifier is the:
options: Product of voltage and current gain
Range of frequencies over which the gain stays within 3 dB of its mid-band value
explanation: BW = f_H − f_L, measured between the half-power (−3 dB) points where gain falls to 0.707 of mid-band gain.

q: The main advantage of FM over AM is:
explanation: Noise mostly affects amplitude; an FM receiver’s limiter removes amplitude variations, so FM gives much better signal-to-noise ratio — at the cost of wider bandwidth.

q: In transmission lines, corona loss increases with:
explanation: Peek’s formula: Pc ∝ (f + 25)(V − Vd)². Loss rises steeply once the operating voltage exceeds the disruptive critical voltage; a bigger conductor diameter raises Vd and reduces corona.

q: The purpose of a step-up transformer is to:
explanation: At a power station, generator voltage (11–22 kV) is stepped up to 132/220/500 kV for transmission; current falls in the same ratio.

q: The open-circuit (no-load) test on a transformer is used to measure:
explanation: At rated voltage with the secondary open, the small no-load current makes copper loss negligible, so the wattmeter reads core loss; it also gives the shunt branch R0 and X0.

q: In a 132 kV three-phase system (line-to-line), the line-to-neutral voltage is approximately:
explanation: V_LN ≈ 76.2 kV

q: Which part is common to both DC machines and AC generators (alternators)?
explanation: Both need a magnetic field produced by a field winding (excited with DC). DC machines have a commutator; alternators feed their rotating field through slip rings.

q: The efficiency of a DC motor is maximum when:
options: Copper losses are greater than iron losses
Copper losses are less than iron losses
explanation: As for any machine, efficiency peaks when variable losses (armature I²R) equal constant losses (iron, friction, windage, shunt-field).

q: A moving-iron instrument can measure:
explanation: The deflecting torque ∝ I², so it is independent of current direction and reads RMS on both AC and DC (with some error on DC from hysteresis).

q: The main function of a Buchholz relay is to:
options: Detect internal (incipient and severe) faults in oil-filled transformers
explanation: Gas released by insulation breakdown or arcing under oil collects in the relay: a slow build-up operates the alarm float, a violent surge operates the trip float.

q: In thermal (steam) power plants, the prime mover is usually a:
explanation: Boiler steam drives a steam turbine coupled to the alternator (Rankine cycle). Gas turbines are the prime movers in gas/combined-cycle plants.

q: The function of a surge tank in a hydroelectric plant is to:
options: Absorb pressure rise (water hammer) when load is rejected
explanation: When the turbine gates close suddenly, the moving water column would cause a dangerous pressure surge in the penstock; the surge tank provides a free surface that absorbs it (and supplies water on sudden load increase).

q: The major disadvantage of a nuclear power plant is:
explanation: Fuel cost per kWh is low and there is no combustion smoke, but spent fuel stays radioactive for thousands of years and needs safe long-term storage; capital cost is also high.

q: A fuse in an electrical circuit is used to:
explanation: The fuse element melts when current exceeds its rating for long enough, opening the circuit and protecting cables and equipment. It does not prevent a fault from occurring — it clears it.

q: The frequency of the voltage generated by an alternator depends on:
explanation: f = PN/120. That is why grid generators run at fixed synchronous speed (e.g. 3000 rpm for 2 poles, 1500 rpm for 4 poles at 50 Hz).

q: In an oil circuit breaker, the arc is extinguished by:
explanation: The arc decomposes the oil into gas (mainly hydrogen) whose high thermal conductivity and pressure cool and de-ionise the arc path. SF₆ breakers use SF₆ gas instead.

q: The relay generally used to detect earth faults (leakage to earth) is a/an:
explanation: An earth-fault relay is fed from the residual connection of CTs (or a core-balance CT) and responds to zero-sequence current, which flows only when current leaks to earth.

q: The main function of a current transformer (CT) is to:
options: Step down current to a standard value (1 A or 5 A) for metering and protection
explanation: A CT isolates instruments and relays from the high-voltage circuit and reduces the line current to 1 A or 5 A. Its secondary must never be opened under load (dangerous voltage).

q: The primary function of a power transformer is to:
options: Step voltage up or down at the same frequency
explanation: A transformer transfers power between circuits by mutual induction, changing voltage and current in the turns ratio; frequency is unchanged and it does not work on steady DC.

q: In a power transformer, leakage flux is minimised by:
explanation: Placing the LV and HV windings concentrically on the same limb (or interleaving sections) keeps them closely coupled, so less flux links only one winding. Laminations reduce eddy loss, not leakage.

q: The main losses that reduce transformer efficiency are:
explanation: A transformer has no moving parts, so its losses are iron loss (hysteresis + eddy, constant) and copper loss (I²R, varies with load²). Efficiency is typically 97–99.5 %.

q: The EMF generated per phase in an alternator (E = 4.44 f Φ N) is directly proportional to:
options: Speed, flux per pole and turns per phase together
explanation: E = 4.44 k f Φ N with f = PN/120, so EMF ∝ speed × flux per pole × turns per phase (times the winding factor).

q: When a synchronous motor runs at constant load and its excitation is adjusted for unity power factor, its armature current is:
explanation: On the V-curve, armature current is lowest at unity power factor; under-excitation makes it draw lagging current and over-excitation leading current, both larger.

q: Compared with a slip-ring motor, the starting torque of a squirrel-cage induction motor is generally:
explanation: The cage rotor has fixed, low resistance, giving low starting torque with high starting current (5–7 × rated). Slip-ring motors add external rotor resistance to get high starting torque.

q: The starting torque of a DC series motor is:
explanation: Field flux is produced by armature current, so torque ∝ Ia² below saturation — the highest starting torque of all DC motors.

q: The back EMF of a DC motor is proportional to:
explanation: Eb = PΦZN/(60A) ∝ ΦN. Back EMF regulates the armature current: Ia = (V − Eb)/Ra.

q: The overall efficiency of a conventional (coal/steam) thermal power plant is typically about:
explanation: Most heat is rejected in the condenser (Rankine cycle limit), so classic plants achieve about 30–35 %; modern supercritical units reach ~40 %+, and combined-cycle gas plants 50–60 %.

q: Arc interruption in a circuit breaker is achieved mainly by:
options: Cooling, lengthening and de-ionising the arc so the gap’s dielectric strength recovers faster than the restriking voltage
explanation: AC arcs are interrupted at a current zero; the breaker wins if the dielectric strength of the gap builds up faster than the transient recovery voltage. High-resistance (cooling, lengthening, splitting) and low-resistance (current-zero) methods both rely on de-ionisation.

q: In a DC motor, torque is directly proportional to:
explanation: T = (PZ/2πA) Φ Ia, so T ∝ Φ Ia. For a shunt motor (Φ constant) T ∝ Ia; for a series motor T ∝ Ia².

q: In a DC motor, the speed is inversely proportional to:
options: Number of armature conductors in parallel paths only
explanation: N ∝ Eb/Φ = (V − IaRa)/Φ. Weakening the field raises speed (field control); for a series motor at light load Φ is small, so speed rises dangerously.

q: The purpose of oil in a transformer is:
explanation: Mineral oil insulates the windings and carries heat to the tank and radiators by convection. Its dielectric strength (BDV) is tested regularly.

q: The slip of an induction motor is given by:
explanation: Slip is the speed difference as a fraction of synchronous speed; rotor frequency = s × f. Typical full-load slip is 2–5 %.

q: The field excitation of a synchronous motor is provided by:
explanation: The rotor field is DC-excited (exciter or static excitation through slip rings, or brushless exciter), so it locks with the rotating stator field at synchronous speed.

q: A lagging power factor is caused by:
explanation: Inductive loads (motors, transformers, chokes) draw magnetising current that lags the voltage; capacitors are added to supply this reactive power locally.

q: An alternator works at maximum efficiency when:
options: Copper losses are greater than iron losses
explanation: As with transformers and DC machines, efficiency is maximum when the load-dependent copper loss equals the constant losses (core, friction, windage, excitation).

q: The primary purpose of a protective relay in a power system is to:
options: Detect faults and initiate circuit-breaker tripping
explanation: A relay senses abnormal conditions from CT/VT signals and closes the trip circuit of the breaker; the breaker then interrupts the fault current.

q: In power factor correction, shunt capacitors are used to:
explanation: Capacitors supply the reactive power that inductive loads need, so the line carries less reactive current — power factor rises, current and I²R losses fall, and voltage improves.

q: The voltage regulation of a transformer depends mainly on:
options: Load current and load power factor
explanation: Regulation ≈ (I·R cosφ ± I·X sinφ)/V: it grows with load and is worst at low lagging power factor; it can be negative at leading power factor.

q: The direction of rotation of a 3-phase induction motor can be reversed by:
explanation: Swapping two lines reverses the phase sequence, which reverses the direction of the rotating magnetic field and hence the rotor.

q: The purpose of power factor correction is to:
options: Reduce line current and losses for the same real power
explanation: For the same kW, I = P/(√3 V cosφ): raising cosφ lowers current, losses, voltage drop and kVA demand charges (WAPDA/DISCOs penalise industrial PF below 0.9).

q: In a synchronous motor with constant excitation, when the load increases the armature current:
explanation: Speed stays synchronous; the rotor falls back by a larger load angle δ, and the stator draws more current to supply the extra power (P = (EV/Xs) sin δ).

q: For maximum power transfer from a DC source to a load, the load resistance must be:
explanation: P = V²R_L/(R_s + R_L)² is maximum at R_L = R_s, giving P_max = V²/(4R_s) at 50 % efficiency. For AC, the load is the complex conjugate of the source impedance.

q: The instrument used to measure very high (insulation) resistance is the:
explanation: A megger applies 500 V–5 kV DC and reads in megohms. A Wheatstone bridge suits medium resistances and a Kelvin double bridge very low ones.

q: The main reason for providing a tap changer on a transformer is to:
explanation: Taps change the effective turns ratio to hold secondary voltage within limits as load and supply vary. On-load tap changers (OLTC) on grid transformers do this without interrupting supply.

q: A transmission line has a sending-end voltage of 220 kV and a receiving-end voltage of 200 kV at full load. The voltage regulation is:
The input power of a balanced 3-phase motor is given by:
explanation: Three-phase real power P = √3 V_L I_L cosφ = 3 V_ph I_ph cosφ. The shaft output is this times the motor efficiency.

q: The function of the governor of a generating unit is to:
explanation: The governor adjusts steam/water/fuel input to keep speed — and therefore frequency — constant as load changes (with a droop of about 4–5 %). Voltage is controlled by the AVR/excitation system.

q: Which instrument measures the real power in an AC circuit?
explanation: A dynamometer wattmeter (current coil in series, pressure coil in parallel) reads V·I·cosφ. An energy meter integrates power over time (kWh).

q: Which conductor material is commonly used for overhead transmission lines?
explanation: Aluminium is lighter and cheaper than copper for the same resistance; steel-cored aluminium (ACSR) adds tensile strength for long spans. WAPDA/NTDC use ACSR (e.g. Rail, Greeley, Lynx).

q: Which type of relay is mainly used for the protection of transmission lines?
explanation: Distance (impedance) relays measure V/I at the relay point; the impedance is proportional to the distance to the fault, giving fast, zone-based selective tripping (zone 1 ≈ 80 % of the line).

q: The armature winding of a large alternator is usually placed on the:
explanation: A stationary armature is easier to insulate for high voltage and can be connected directly to the busbars without sliding contacts; only the low-power DC field rotates.

q: The primary purpose of a circuit breaker is to:
explanation: A breaker can make and break normal load current and, on a relay trip signal, interrupt fault currents of many kA. Its rating includes breaking capacity in kA or MVA.

q: A device that converts mechanical energy into electrical energy is called a:
explanation: A generator works on electromagnetic induction (Faraday, 1831): conductors moving through a magnetic field have an EMF induced in them. A motor does the reverse.

q: Determine the total charge entering a terminal between t = 1 s and t = 2 s if the current is i = (3t² − t) A.
Using the passive sign convention, the reactive power Q absorbed by a capacitor is:
explanation: Q = V·I·sinθ with θ = angle of V relative to I; for a capacitor the current leads, θ = −90°, so Q = −V²/Xc < 0. A capacitor absorbs negative vars — i.e. it supplies reactive power to inductive loads.

reported.note: The source key said Q > 0. Under the standard (passive) convention a capacitor absorbs negative reactive power, Q < 0 — corrected.

q: The capacitance of a variable air capacitor is maximum when:
options: Both sets of plates are fully meshed
The movable plates half overlap the fixed plates
The movable plates are most widely separated from the fixed plates
explanation: C = εA/d, and the effective area A is the overlapping area. It is largest when the movable vanes are fully meshed with the fixed vanes.

q: Large modern synchronous generators generate at a terminal voltage of approximately:
explanation: Generator stator insulation limits terminal voltage to roughly 11–27 kV (e.g. 22 kV at Tarbela units); generator step-up transformers then raise it to 220/500 kV.

q: The capacitance of a parallel-plate capacitor (plate area A, separation d, permittivity ε) is:
explanation: Capacitance rises with plate area and permittivity and falls with separation: C = ε₀εᵣA/d.

q: An integrator is an op-amp circuit whose output is proportional to the ______ of the input signal.
explanation: With R at the input and C in feedback, v_out = −(1/RC)∫v_in dt. Swapping R and C gives a differentiator.

q: At ω = 4 rad/s, the phasor impedance of a 0.5 H inductor is:
explanation: = j2 Ω

q: A fully charged 50 Ah battery rated for 10 h discharge is discharged at a steady 5 A. It will last about:
solution: = 10 h (at the rated rate; higher currents give less than rated Ah)
explanation: = 10 h (at the rated rate; higher currents give less than rated Ah)

q: An alternating current completes 100 cycles in 0.1 s. Its frequency is:
explanation: = 1000 Hz = 1 kHz

q: Pakistan’s ±660 kV Matiari–Lahore HVDC line is designed to transmit about:
explanation: The 878 km bipole (commissioned 2021, built under CPEC) carries up to 4000 MW from the southern coal and wind generation to Lahore.

q: In a Y-Y system, a line voltage of 220 V corresponds to a phase voltage of:
The average power in an AC network (period T) is:
explanation: Average power is the mean of instantaneous power p(t) = v(t)i(t) over one period; for sinusoids it equals V_rms·I_rms·cosφ.

q: The equivalent conductance of N resistors connected in parallel is:
explanation: In parallel, currents add for the same voltage: I = V(G₁ + G₂ + …), so conductances add (the dual of series resistances adding).

q: How much energy does a 100 W bulb consume in four hours?
explanation: = 400 Wh = 0.4 kWh (units)

q: An isolating transformer has a turns ratio of:
explanation: It gives galvanic isolation (for safety or noise) without changing the voltage, so primary and secondary turns are equal.

q: When a capacitor is connected to an AC supply, the current:
options: Is in phase with the voltage
Leads the voltage by π/2 rad
explanation: i = C dv/dt: the current is greatest when the voltage is changing fastest (at its zero crossing), so it leads by 90° (π/2 rad).

q: ______ materials have low reluctance and are used as magnetic screens to protect equipment from external magnetic fields.
explanation: Flux prefers the low-reluctance path through a high-permeability shield (mu-metal, soft iron), diverting it around the enclosed space. Copper and aluminium shield only against changing fields via eddy currents.

q: What is the voltage across a 3 µF capacitor if the charge on one plate is 0.12 mC?
For a BJT in the active region, the relationship between collector current Ic and emitter current Ie is:
explanation: Ie = Ic + Ib, so Ic = αIe with α ≈ 0.98–0.995: the collector current is slightly less than the emitter current.

q: cos(ωt − 90°) equals:
explanation: cos(θ − 90°) = cos θ cos 90° + sin θ sin 90° = sin θ. So a sine wave lags the cosine wave by 90°.

q: A 24 V DC source is connected to 4 Ω and 8 Ω resistors in series. The current is:
A series RLC circuit has R = 10 Ω, L = 0.1 H and C = 100 µF on a 100 V, 50 Hz supply. Its impedance is approximately:
explanation: ≈ 10.0 Ω (almost at resonance, f₀ ≈ 50.3 Hz)

q: A 500 MW thermal plant operates at 38 % overall efficiency using coal of calorific value 25 MJ/kg. Its coal consumption per hour is about:
explanation: ≈ 189,500 kg/h (≈ 190 tonnes per hour)

reported.note: The source key gave 18,960 kg — ten times too small (a power-of-ten slip). The correct figure is ≈ 189,500 kg/h — options corrected.

q: A 100 MVA, 220/33 kV power transformer is protected by a differential relay (CTs 1000:5 on HV, 5000:5 on LV). The purpose of this relay is to:
options: Detect internal faults within the transformer zone
explanation: Differential protection compares (ratio- and phase-corrected) currents entering and leaving the protected zone; any significant difference means a fault inside the zone, which it trips instantly. External (through) faults are ignored.

q: The primary purpose of an economiser in a thermal power plant is to:
options: Preheat the boiler feedwater using heat from the flue gases
explanation: The economiser recovers heat from the exit flue gases to warm the feedwater before the boiler drum, raising boiler efficiency and saving fuel. (The air preheater does the same for combustion air.)

q: In an AM wave, the maximum and minimum envelope voltages are 10 V and 2 V. The modulation index is:
Which method is most suitable for analysing multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) control systems?
options: Nyquist plot of a single loop
explanation: State-space models ẋ = Ax + Bu, y = Cx + Du handle many inputs and outputs (and initial conditions) in one matrix framework; Bode, root locus and Nyquist are single-loop tools.

q: Which smart-grid function is primarily responsible for real-time demand response and load balancing?
explanation: DSM shifts or curtails consumer load in response to price or grid signals. PMUs provide synchronised measurements for wide-area monitoring, not demand control.

q: Which power-electronic converter converts AC to an adjustable (variable) DC voltage?
explanation: Delaying the firing angle α of the thyristors varies the average output: for a full converter Vdc = (2Vm/π) cos α.

q: Which control technique is commonly used in switch-mode power supplies to regulate the output voltage efficiently?
explanation: PWM varies the duty cycle of the switch (e.g. buck: Vo = D·Vin). The switch is either fully on or off, so losses are low and efficiency is high (85–95 %).

q: In digital signal processing, the Z-transform is mainly used to:
options: Convert continuous-time signals into discrete time
Analyse and design discrete-time linear time-invariant systems
explanation: It is the discrete-time counterpart of the Laplace transform: difference equations become algebraic, and poles inside the unit circle mean a stable digital filter. Aliasing is prevented by an anti-aliasing filter and adequate sampling rate.

q: Which method is commonly used for large-scale load-flow studies because of its fast (quadratic) convergence?
explanation: Newton–Raphson converges in a few iterations almost independently of system size; Gauss–Seidel is simple but needs many iterations on large systems. Fast-decoupled load flow is a simplified NR.

q: Why is a DC series motor unsuitable where constant speed is needed under varying load?
options: It needs an external regulator for its field
Its speed varies widely with load
explanation: Flux depends on load current, so N ∝ 1/Φ changes greatly with load — and the motor races dangerously at no load. Shunt motors give nearly constant speed.

q: If the field winding of a running DC shunt motor opens, the motor will:
options: Speed up dangerously (only residual flux remains)
Stop because armature current falls to zero
explanation: With only residual flux, back EMF collapses, armature current surges and N ∝ V/Φ rises sharply. Field-failure protection is fitted to trip the motor.

q: In frequency modulation, the bandwidth of the transmitted signal is determined mainly by:
options: The frequency deviation and the highest modulating frequency
explanation: Carson’s rule: BW ≈ 2(Δf + f_m). Broadcast FM: 2(75 + 15) = 180 kHz (200 kHz channels).

q: When applying Thevenin’s theorem, the Thevenin equivalent resistance is found by:
options: Measuring the total resistance with all sources active
Removing the load, deactivating independent sources and finding the resistance seen from the load terminals
explanation: Voltage sources are replaced by shorts and current sources by opens (dependent sources stay; then use a test source). Alternatively R_th = V_oc/I_sc.

q: The primary reason for using FACTS devices in modern power grids is to:
explanation: FACTS devices (SVC, STATCOM, TCSC, UPFC) use power electronics to control voltage, line impedance and phase angle quickly, increasing transfer capability and damping oscillations.

q: Series capacitors are installed in long AC transmission lines mainly to:
options: Compensate the line’s series inductive reactance, increasing power transfer and stability
Raise the receiving-end voltage at no load
explanation: P = VsVr sin δ / X: series capacitors reduce the net reactance X, raising the power limit, reducing voltage drop and improving stability (with care for sub-synchronous resonance).

q: HVDC transmission is preferred for very long distances mainly because it:
options: Can be tapped easily at many points
Is cheaper to build at any distance
Has lower losses and no reactive/stability limit beyond the break-even distance
explanation: DC has no charging current, skin effect or stability limit and needs only two conductors (bipole). Converter stations are costly, so it pays beyond the break-even distance (≈ 600–800 km overhead).

q: Distance protection is preferred for high-voltage transmission lines because it:
options: Determines the fault location by measuring impedance
explanation: Impedance to the fault is proportional to distance, so zones can be set (Z1 ≈ 80 % instantaneous, Z2/Z3 time-delayed backup). It needs both CT and VT inputs.

q: In a nuclear power plant, the primary function of the moderator is to:
options: Slow down fast neutrons to sustain the chain reaction
Act as coolant and transfer heat to the turbine
explanation: Fission neutrons are fast; slowing them (ordinary/heavy water, graphite) to thermal energies greatly raises the chance of further U-235 fission. Control rods (boron, cadmium) absorb neutrons.

q: In a linear time-invariant system, observability means that:
options: The system can be controlled with a single input
All state variables can be determined from the output measurements
The system is stable for all inputs
explanation: Kalman test: the observability matrix [C; CA; …; CAⁿ⁻¹] has full rank n. Controllability is the dual property (all states can be driven by the inputs).

q: Which feature lets a smart grid integrate renewable energy sources efficiently?
options: Energy storage with real-time monitoring and demand response
explanation: Solar and wind are variable; storage, forecasting and demand response balance them in real time so they can be absorbed without curtailment or instability.

q: A single-phase induction motor needs an auxiliary starting arrangement because:
options: A single winding produces only a pulsating, not a rotating, magnetic field
It cannot run at high speed
explanation: A pulsating field equals two equal, opposite rotating fields, giving zero net starting torque. A split-phase or capacitor-start winding creates the phase shift needed to start.

q: In a three-phase induction motor, the rotor rotates because of:
options: Interaction between the rotating magnetic field and the currents it induces in the rotor
explanation: The stator’s rotating field induces EMF and current in the rotor conductors (transformer action); the force on these currents drags the rotor after the field — Lenz’s law.

q: The main advantage of a ring-main distribution system over a radial system is:
options: Improved reliability and continuity of supply
explanation: Each load point can be fed from two directions, so a faulted section can be isolated while the rest stays energised; voltage drop is also lower. It costs more and needs more complex protection.

q: A linear control system is stable if all poles of its characteristic equation:
options: Have negative real parts (lie in the left half-plane)
Lie in the right half of the s-plane
explanation: Each pole contributes e^(pt) to the response; it decays only if Re(p) < 0. Poles on the jω axis give sustained oscillation (marginal stability).

q: Which law states that the line integral of the magnetic field around a closed path equals the total current enclosed?
explanation: ∮H·dl = I_enclosed (Maxwell added the displacement current term). It gives, e.g., H = I/(2πr) around a long straight conductor.

q: Which semiconductor device is commonly used in high-power controlled rectifier applications?
explanation: SCRs handle thousands of volts and amperes with low conduction loss and are line-commutated in AC–DC converters (including HVDC valves). MOSFETs suit lower-power, high-frequency switching.

q: Which protection scheme is commonly used for detecting internal faults in a power transformer?
explanation: Biased (percentage) differential protection with harmonic restraint (to ignore inrush current) is the main protection for large transformers, backed up by Buchholz and overcurrent relays.

q: Which type of relay operates when the impedance seen by it falls below a set value?
explanation: A fault reduces the V/I ratio seen at the relay; if it falls inside the zone setting the distance relay operates.

q: The primary function of a protective relay in a power system is to:
explanation: Relays monitor current, voltage, frequency, etc., and when a fault is detected they trip the circuit breaker to isolate the faulty part.

q: Which part of a DC machine carries the current that interacts with the field to convert electrical energy into mechanical energy (in a motor)?
explanation: Torque is produced on the current-carrying armature conductors in the field (F = BIL); the commutator keeps that torque unidirectional.

q: The main purpose of a modulator in a communication system is to:
options: Impress the information signal onto a carrier
explanation: Modulation shifts the message to a high-frequency carrier so it can be radiated by practical antennas and many channels can share the spectrum (frequency division).

q: Which device is used to protect power distribution systems from overcurrent?
explanation: Breakers (and fuses) interrupt current above a safe limit; in distribution, MCBs/MCCBs and relay-operated breakers on 11 kV feeders do this.

q: The primary purpose of a step-down transformer in a distribution system is to:
explanation: Grid voltage (132/11 kV) is stepped down by distribution transformers (11 kV/400 V) to the 400/230 V supplied to consumers.

q: The main advantage of digital signal processing over analog processing is:
explanation: Discrete levels are regenerated without accumulating noise, results are exactly repeatable, and the same hardware can be reprogrammed. The trade-offs are sampling, quantisation and processing delay.

q: Which element of a control system processes the error signal and generates the control action?
explanation: The controller (e.g. PID) acts on e = r − y to produce the actuating signal for the plant; the sensor measures the output for feedback.

q: Which power-electronic device is commonly used as a fast switch in DC circuits?
explanation: A power MOSFET is voltage-controlled (almost no gate current) and switches very fast, so it is the usual switch in DC–DC converters and SMPS. A diode cannot be turned on/off by a control signal.

q: In a thermal power plant, the main energy conversion sequence is:
explanation: Fuel’s chemical energy becomes heat in the boiler, steam drives the turbine (mechanical), and the alternator converts that to electrical energy.

q: Which type of power is measured in volt-amperes (VA)?
explanation: S = V_rms·I_rms (VA, kVA, MVA). Active power P is in W and reactive power Q in VAr; S² = P² + Q². Transformers are rated in kVA/MVA.

q: The electrical power in a DC circuit is given by:
explanation: P = VI = I²R = V²/R (watts).

q: The instantaneous power in an inductor is proportional to the:
options: Product of the instantaneous current and its rate of change
Square of the rate of change of current
explanation: p = v·i = L·i·(di/dt) = d/dt(½Li²): it is positive while the stored energy grows and negative while it is returned to the circuit.

q: For a connected network with b branches, n nodes and l independent loops, the fundamental theorem of network topology gives:
explanation: A tree has n − 1 branches; each of the remaining links closes one independent loop, so l = b − n + 1, i.e. b = l + n − 1.

q: For large induction motors, typical slip between no load and full load is about:
explanation: Large machines have low rotor resistance, so full-load slip is small (≈ 1–2 %), giving high efficiency (rotor copper loss = s × air-gap power). Small motors run at 3–6 % slip.
